title: FCA: file-qualified symbol identity in convention checking
description:
## Motivation

Codex review of sutra/v1/12 found that `SymbolAttrs.name` (qualified_name) isn't globally unique across files. Two symbols named `process` in different files would both be exempted if one is listed in `conventions.exempt`. Same ambiguity in `ConventionViolation` — downstream consumers can't disambiguate.

## What to build

Add file path to `SymbolAttrs` so convention checking can use file-qualified identity. Update exemption matching and violation reporting to use the file-qualified key.

## Changes

1. Add `file: String` field to `SymbolAttrs`
2. Update `extract_symbol_attrs` to pass through the file path (it already receives `file_path: &str`)
3. Update `FcaEngine::check()` exemption matching to use `file::name` or similar composite key
4. Add `file: String` to `ConventionViolation` for downstream disambiguation
5. Update `ConventionExemption` to support file-qualified symbol names (e.g. `src/foo.rs::process`)
6. Regression test: two symbols with same name in different files, exempt one, assert the other still violates

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `SymbolAttrs` carries file path
- [ ] Exemptions match on file-qualified identity, not bare name
- [ ] `ConventionViolation` includes file path
- [ ] Regression test: same-name symbols in different files, exemption scoped correctly
- [ ] Existing tests still pass
